## v0.3.111 — hotfix

### Fixed: PostToolUse hook panic that silently dropped telemetry
`post_observe::check_duplicate` sliced the observation-log tail at a raw byte offset that could land inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character (box-drawing '═', printed constantly by agent panes), panicking the hook. Because the hook exits 0 while panicking, Claude Code reported only a non-blocking failure and the counterfactual observation was silently dropped on affected tool calls. The tail start now snaps to a char boundary. Regression test included.

Upgrade recommended for all installs.

### Install / update
```bash
precc update    # or: curl -fsSL https://peria.ai/install.sh | bash
```

## v0.3.110

### New: `precc receipt` — auditable, reversible decision ledger
See what PRECC rewrote, why, and how to undo it. `precc receipt [--since 24h] [--limit N] [--json]` prints a per-decision ledger — each rewrite is content-addressed and reversible via `precc undo <id>` — grouped by decision class. `--json` for agents/dashboards. Measured token totals stay in `precc savings`.

Also available as the `/receipt` slash command in the Claude Code plugin.

### Install
```bash
curl -fsSL https://peria.ai/install.sh | bash
precc init
```

## PRECC v0.3.108

### Compression routing: prefer lean-ctx over nushell in the cold-start fallback
Ground-truth measurement showed lean-ctx output compression is strongly
net-positive (~+49% on measured commands) while nushell is weak-to-negative
(−20% to −30% net on some command classes). The static/cold-start fallback was
trying **nushell first**, so the weaker backend preempted lean-ctx for every
command it could handle — dragging the default path net-negative on installs
that have no per-class measurements yet (the adaptive net-loss guard only
governs the learned pick, not this fallback).

Fallback reordered to lean-ctx → nushell → lowfat → compression-prompt → rtk.
Verbose commands (grep/find/ls/…) now route to lean-ctx instead of nushell.
Carries the v0.3.107 Windows console-window fix for anyone not yet on it.

## PRECC v0.3.107

### Fix: Windows console window flashing every few minutes
PRECC's background helpers were launched without the Windows `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`
flag, so each briefly popped a console window. With the background `precc-learner`
daemon now running reliably, its periodic helpers (update poll + anonymized
telemetry via `curl`, liveness check via `tasklist`, the daemon self-respawn) and
the per-command savings re-run (`bash -c`) each flashed a console — the "every
few minutes" flicker reported on Windows.

All subprocess spawns now route through a shared `proc_util::no_window()` helper
that sets `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on Windows. Windows-only, behaviour-preserving — no
change on macOS/Linux.

## PRECC v0.3.106

Version bump so installs already on 0.3.105 pick up the per-(class, mode)
`class_mode_savings` telemetry (Tier 2 fleet-prior data collection). That field
shipped in the 0.3.105 re-cut, but `precc update` treats a same-version re-cut as
"already current" and won't refresh installs that updated to 0.3.105 before the
re-cut — this bump reaches them.

No functional change versus the latest 0.3.105 binary: measured-only savings
headline + output-compression ratio, adaptive mode selection (net-loss guard,
rtk sampling, cold-start prior), and the fleet mode-prior telemetry.

## PRECC v0.3.105

### Adaptive compression: cold-start prior
New installs no longer cold-start on the weakest backend. The mode selector now
consults a compiled-in best-mode-per-class **prior** when a machine has no
locally-learned entry for a command class yet — seeding the measured, lossless
wins (`git status|diff|log|show|branch`, `ls -la|-l`, `ps aux|-ef` → `rtk`,
which compresses that output ~84–99%). The locally-learned snapshot always
overrides the prior, and the net-loss guard self-corrects any class where a mode
underperforms on a given machine. Existing installs benefit on upgrade too.

This ships the fleet's lesson to every install from command #1, instead of each
machine re-discovering it from scratch (the cause of the low measured ratio on
fresh installs). A fleet-derived, self-updating prior is scoped for a follow-up
(docs/mode-selector-fleet-prior.md).

## PRECC v0.3.104

### Honest, measured savings reporting
- The site/fleet headline now reports **measured** output-compression savings (ground-truth before/after token counts) instead of multiplier-based pillar estimates. The fabricated lean-ctx `wrap × 350` headline is gone; the public number reconciles with its per-version table.
- A **stratified projection** (measured per-class rates × observed traffic) is shown alongside the measured number, and a transition note explains the change for existing users.
- **Counterfactual failure preventions** (wrong-dir corrections, mined fixes) are credited as a clearly-labelled estimate at **measured per-event rates** (~290 tok/wrong-dir, ~170/mined — re-derived from real session-log error cycles), separate from the measured headline.

### Adaptive compression mode selection
- **Net-loss guard:** the selector never picks a compression mode whose measured net savings is ≤ 0 for a command class. When no mode is net-positive, compression is suppressed (raw output) rather than applying a backend that inflates output.
- **rtk-as-sampled-candidate:** rtk (previously preempted by nushell and never measured) now runs on a small deterministic sample of eligible commands so it accrues measurements and can be selected for the classes where it wins big and losslessly (git/ps/ls). Tunable via `PRECC_RTK_SAMPLE_RATE` (0 disables).

These make the per-class adaptive selector deliver "best backend per situation, revisited as data accumulates" on measured data.

Fixes diet budget over-credit (estimate now mirrors apply guards; journalctl --no-pager no longer over-credited). Nudge functional-core refactor (behaviour-preserving). Adds nightly mutation, cargo-fuzz, and Miri CI; property/metamorphic/differential/grammar-fuzz test suites.
